title: Recited lists (number words, boxed compass, hours, months, days, planets, zodiac, letter names, Roman numerals, World Clock city ring; English and German) at every start letter as exact running keys: any-tableau gate, 666,993 keyword tableaux, one hidden alphabet
k4_result: 0 hits. 270 lists give 740 key texts (forwards and letters reversed) and 387,800 start letters. Any-tableau gate (R->P at letters 28 and 66 needs equal key letters, 22 other clue pairs need different ones): 7,017 starts pass (1.8%), 4,400 different 24-letter keys; the boxed compass from ENE fails it (key letters T and S), and from their own first letter only 2 forward lists pass (English numbers 60 down to 1, German ordinals 97 down to 1). Keyword tableaux (666,993 alphabets x 5 layouts x Vigenere/Beaufort/variant/Beaufort with negated key x key letter valued on A-Z, KRYPTOS or the tableau alphabet x 26 shifts): 0 starts give 24 of 24. One hidden alphabet (idea 93's 25 models; 17,026 linear systems solved): 0 survivors, 0 undecided. Closest on plain A-Z/KRYPTOS tableaux: 10 of 24 clue letters (7 settings), reading is gibberish (big model -8.03, word cover 0.04; English needs -5.1). Nothing reached the reading stage.
controls: 20 shuffled K4s, identical procedure, all lists and all alphabets: 0 tableau hits and 0 hidden-alphabet survivors in 20 of 20. Closest on A-Z/KRYPTOS: 9 (8 controls), 10 (11), 11 (1); K4's 10 is the median. Gate: the 5 controls that happen to have a repeated clue pair pass 554-8,723 starts (K4 7,017); the 15 without one pass 33,257-85,233.
planted: 5/5: boxed compass from ENE on a dictionary tableau (true Quagmire III, alphabet KIPPY keyed-columnar; 97/97 letters); the same key on a random hidden alphabet (found among 387,800 starts, 68/97 letters forced, alphabet recovered); EINS ZWEI DREI on the KRYPTOS tableau, Beaufort, key on A-Z, shift 3 (97/97); months letter-reversed, variant, alphabet SERIFIC, key on KRYPTOS, shift 11 (97/97); World Clock ring from BERLIN on a hidden alphabet with A-Z key values (81/97)
scope_limits: Only the 270 lists as written in kryptos/idea158_lists.py, letters run together without spaces, one key letter per text letter, the key starting somewhere in the list and running on (no restart per word or row, no skipping, no key shorter than the text repeated except lists that naturally come round). Spellings: one per list plus FUENF/FUNF; no ZWO, no AND below 100 variants beyond those listed, no half or quarter compass points, no letter names such as AY BEE CEE, no other languages. World Clock ring uses the partly reconstructed 1989 plates (17 of 24 facets are not fully verified) and the post-1997 plates. Tableaux: keyword alphabets from the 666,993 list in 5 layouts, or one fully hidden alphabet in idea 93's models; not two different hidden alphabets, no transposition before or after, no second layer. The gate result (98.2% of starts impossible) holds for every tableau with distinct rows and columns, but the 7,017 starts that pass it are only closed for the tableaux above. Clue positions taken as exact.

negative.hypothesis: The K4 key is a list anyone can recite (counting words, boxing the compass, hours, months, days, planets, letter names, Roman numerals, the World Clock's city ring; English or German), used from some start letter as a running key on a keyword tableau or one hidden alphabet.
negative.scope: 270 lists -> 740 key texts (forwards, said backwards, letters reversed), all 387,800 start letters. (1) Any Latin-square tableau: equal/different key-letter gate from the 24 clue letters. (2) 666,993 keyword alphabets (A-Z, KRYPTOS, dictionary, transposition-mixed) x 5 layouts x Vigenere/Beaufort/variant/negated-key Beaufort x key valued on A-Z, KRYPTOS or the tableau alphabet x 26 shifts, exact 24/24 by hash join (4.0e14 settings). (3) One hidden alphabet: numeric key, true Quagmire III and II, hidden alphabet on one side, exact mod 26 with distinct places.
negative.outcome: Dead: 0 exact hits on keyword tableaux and 0 hidden-alphabet survivors; 380,783 of 387,800 starts (98.2%) are impossible on any tableau, among them the boxed compass from ENE; closest 10/24 on A-Z/KRYPTOS (controls: 20 shuffled K4s, 0 hits and 0 survivors each, closest 9-11, median 10; planted 5/5)

follow_ups: The any-tableau gate is free and strong for any KNOWN key text (it removes 98% of starts on K4): run it over the large book corpora earlier ideas scored only on A-Z/KRYPTOS (Carter, KJV and the rest, if the texts are in the repository) to list the few starts that are possible on SOME tableau, then close those with the idea-93 hidden-alphabet solve.

Recited list restarted at every word or carved row instead of running on (ONE for word 1, TWO for word 2 ...; or the compass point N+k for row k): the key letter then depends on unknown word breaks, so test it with the clue words' own breaks (EAST|NORTHEAST, BERLIN|CLOCK) and the gate.
